units.author: propwatch_ledger
units.text: As promised, checked twice. Finding 1: the Holm was not bought by Ardent Vale directly. The land registry shows a sale eighteen months ago to Fernhollow Nominees Ltd, a company formed six weeks before the purchase. Finding 2: Fernhollow transferred the title to Ardent Vale Holdings eleven days later, for no stated price. Finding 3: Fernhollow was dissolved the following spring. Reference numbers below.

units.author: propwatch_ledger
units.text: To be clear about what this means, before anyone runs with it: buying through a nominee is common when a wealthy buyer doesn't want the seller to know who they are and put the price up. It tells us Ardent Vale wanted the purchase quiet. It does not tell us why. I'd say the same about a farmer buying a field next to his own.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: A shell company formed for one purchase and then dissolved. On an island. In secret. And we're supposed to believe it's for a nice house? Ledger has just done more journalism than the Courier in a month. I'm sending this to my list tonight. Do your research, people, this is how they hide things in plain sight.

units.author: propwatch_ledger
units.text: Gil, please don't send it with that framing. I've said what it means and what it doesn't. 'In secret' is wrong; it's on the public registry, which is how I found it. If you share it, share all three findings and my note, not just the word 'shell'.

units.author: skeptic_planner
units.text: I've checked the title references against the planning file and they're consistent: the clearance application was made in Ardent Vale's name, after the transfer. So the finding holds. Nominee purchases of land are ordinary; I see one every few months in the district. The scale of this clearance is the unusual part. The purchase is not.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Thank you both. This is what a sourced post looks like. I'd ask that nobody attempts to find or post the names of individual directors or of the people behind the nominee company; companies are fair game, people are not. Pell.

units.author: retired_teacher
units.text: A small historical note, since the Holm keeps being described as 'empty'. It was a working place for decades: the curing station employed forty women some summers, and my class of 1991 did a whole project on it. It was empty only after people stopped needing it. I suspect whoever buys it now simply has a use for it that we haven't been told.

units.title: The Holm notice says more than the Courier printed...
units.author: hollow_signal
units.text: There's a screenshot of the Kittering Holm planning notice going round tonight. Same reference, same council header. The description line reads 'total vegetation clearance to facilitate a designated evacuation site'. That's not what's on the Courier's page. Evacuation of whom? From what? I'm not posting it. People who've seen it know what it means.

units.author: skeptic_orla
units.text: Source? You've described a picture you won't show, of a document anyone can read on the council portal in thirty seconds. If the real notice says 'total vegetation clearance, Kittering Holm' and the screenshot says more, the screenshot's been edited. That's the dull explanation and it'll be the right one.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: I've been sent it too, by a subscriber, an hour ago. I'm not posting it until I've had a proper look in daylight, because I do have standards whatever Orla thinks. But I'll say this: the formatting looks right. Same font. Same reference layout. Just asking questions, but why would anyone fake a council notice?

units.author: gilliver_teen
units.text: evacuation site lol. so when the big one comes we all get in the chippy van and drive into the sea? genuinely the holm doesnt even have a toilet. whoever made that picture has never been on a boat

units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: I keep turning the phrase over, which I suspect was the point of it. 'Designated evacuation site'. It's the language of a leaflet, not of a planning notice, which as far as I know never says why you're doing anything, only what. I'll wait for someone like the planning watcher to look in daylight. It's three in the morning, and everything sounds true at three.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: Why would anyone fake a council notice? Because you can do it on your phone in two minutes and people like you will post it. That's why.

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: 07:15, day three. Overnight visibility at the station fell to 30 m and stayed under 100 m from 21:00 to 06:00. Fog signal sounded continuously. Air 3.6 C, dew point 3.6 C, sixty hours now at or near saturation. Pressure 1034 hPa, the high hasn't budged. For the enthusiasts: this is the longest fog spell my station has logged since I put it up. Wife is less enthusiastic.

units.author: gilliver_lamp
units.text: Thank you for the numbers. I have kept the lamp lit in the window all three nights, as usual, and I think it has never looked so small. The postman came to the door at eleven this morning and said he had walked the whole of Harbour Road by the sound of the water. Please tell your wife a cup of cocoa helps with fog signals.

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: 20:00, still 3.2 C and saturated, visibility 40 m. Cocoa delivered, Maud, and gratefully received. Outlook from my own charts: a weak front edging in from the west in three or four days. Until then, more of the same. One oddity: the station's wind sensor hasn't registered a single gust over 3 km/h in 48 hours. That's still for the Sound.

units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: Day three. Power off in Lisle west when I got up, so I commuted in the dark, shaved by torch and left with one side of my face better than the other. Ferry 33 minutes late. A woman next to me knitted the entire crossing and got a sleeve done. That's how long it took. A sleeve.

units.author: lisle_crew_ada
units.text: that was Mrs Penrose, she knits on every crossing, she's done three jumpers this autumn... the evening boats have been all right from my end, slow but no bother. ha, anyway, I'll have the pier lights on early tonight, Ewan, so you can see your way up

units.title: Power cut, Lisle west, this morning.
units.author: retired_teacher
units.text: For anyone on Lisle who hasn't heard: the power went off in the west of the island just before six this morning and came back for most of us around half past nine. Engineers came over on the first boat. The school ran on emergency lighting; I'm told the children loved it. Eleven houses on Chapel Row are still off.

units.author: lineman_tess
units.text: I was on that job, so: a joint on the underground cable under Chapel Row let in water and failed. We put in a temporary link to get most people back, and the last eleven got reconnected after lunch. Permanent fix next week, with letters first. Nothing to do with the fog, just an old joint. Sorry for the cold breakfast.

units.author: retired_teacher
units.text: Thank you, that's very clear, and thank you for coming over in this. Chapel Row had their lights back by two, I'm told, and Mrs Penrose's kettle by five past. One small note: it's 'fewer than twelve houses', not 'less', if anyone is writing it up for the parish newsletter.

units.author: gilliver_lamp
units.text: I asked about the village yesterday afternoon. Nobody I know was down on the slip that night, and the chippy was shut by ten. My mother used to tell us children never to go to the foot of the slip after dark, nor in fog, and never to wait there for a boat, but to wait at the top under the light. I expect someone was not told.

units.author: gilliver_teen
units.text: new business idea. slipway ghost tours, five quid, meet at the chippy, bring a torch and a long coat, i'll do the hailing myself. kerris can do the scary voice. first one's free if you can tell me the height of the ghost to the nearest inch

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: I have removed the post above, which mocked a named member of the ferry crew. Teasing about the weather is one thing; making a joke of someone who was doing her job in difficult conditions is another. I won't remove it a second time without a longer word. Pell.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: Your mother's rule is a good one, and I suspect it's also the explanation. A visitor, or a teenager, or someone from Lisle who didn't know better, goes to the foot of the slip to see the boat come in. The boat shouts at them through a loud-hailer, which is quite frightening, and they freeze and then go. I'd still like the street lights fixed.

units.author: sb_lostcat
units.text: Looked under every van on the market car park last night. Found: one hubcap, a child's shoe, and an extremely offended tabby who was not Pebble. Today a lady came into the shop because of the poster in the window and said she'd seen 'a little grey thing' near the allotments on Rope Walk. I'll go after closing. Thank you for all the kind messages.

units.author: sb_bins
units.text: I live on Rope Walk and walk past the allotments every morning to look at my uncollected recycling. I will keep an eye out for a small grey cat with one white sock. If she is living among the milk bottles on my step, she is welcome to them. Bernard (Rope Walk)

units.author: sb_bins
units.text: Council notice this morning: 'we know some residents in Rope Walk were missed again and apologise; the round has been added to the catch-up list'. So we are now on a list. Not a round. A list. I have lived on Rope Walk for thirty-one years and I have never been on a list. I intend to be taken off it by Friday. Bernard (Rope Walk)

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Bernard, I can confirm as a retired council clerk that the 'catch-up list' is a real thing and is generally done the next working day. I also confirm that being on it is no reflection on Rope Walk. If it isn't done by Friday, I'll give you the waste team's direct number. Pell.

units.title: anyone know brackwater woods?? doing a LIVE investigation
units.author: nightscream_vlog
units.text: guys. the brackwater knocks are going viral on LowBand and nobody's actually gone out there LIVE. im doing a full investigation, thermal cam, spirit box, the works, stream link in bio. need someone who knows the paths and where the pumping house is. insane opportunity, ill credit you on stream

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: Here's what you'll find in Brackwater Woods at night: mud, a locked gate, and a gamekeeper who'll take your number plate. Spirit box. Grow up. If you fall down the dam bank, I'm not chipping in for the rescue.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Moved to Local Oddities. A reminder that the Brackwater estate has asked people not to enter the woods or the reservoir grounds after dark, and that the access road is icy this week. Please do not use this board to organise trespass. Pell.

units.author: retired_teacher
units.text: Lisle, clearly, from the kitchen. Every thirty seconds for three nights. I've stopped hearing it in the day and started hearing it in my sleep, and last night I dreamed I was taking the register and every child answered with a fog signal. I shall be glad of the front.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Tollinby, east side: yes, faintly, when the dishwasher's off. My youngest has started counting it like sheep and is asleep by forty. Best sleep aid I've had all year. I may write to the coastguard and ask them to keep it.

units.title: slipway: interim notice
units.author: harbourmaster_quill
units.text: Interim notice, while I wait for the parish to agree a proper sign: the Gilliver slipway is closed to the public after dark and during ferry arrivals and departures (byelaw 14). I have hung a temporary notice on the rail at the top and put a lamp beside it. Please wait in the shelter. Thank you, and thank you to the crew for reporting.

units.author: ferry_skipper_odell
units.text: Thank you. Since a few people have asked me on the boat: no, I don't have a theory, and I'm not going to make one up. A person was on the slip in fog when they shouldn't have been, and I held off until it was safe. That's all a deck log is for. Logged it, carried on.

units.author: deckhand_finn
units.text: half the boat asked me about it today, I said it was a seal that learned to stand up. one old boy said he'd seen that before. skipper gave me a look. ok fine it was a person, probably. lamp by the sign's a good idea, it's like a little lighthouse for people who cant read

units.author: ferry_mate_kerris
units.text: It wasn't a seal, Finn, and I'd rather you didn't tell passengers it was. It was a person at the very end where the water starts, tall, dark coat, no light, and they didn't move when hailed. I've said that four times now and I'll keep saying it the same way. The lamp is good. Thank you, Quill.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: quill's lamp is the one from my shop window, on loan, she didnt ask and i didnt mind. it'll stay on all night. finn, kerris is right, dont wind up the passengers, the old boys will have it all round the pub by friday as fact. lads keep it working talk on here

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Collected my marker from Quill. Went out to the near string for an hour at first light while it was thinner, nine lobsters, kept four. Couldn't see the Holm at all, but you could hear the saws start up at half seven, faint through it. Then the fog came back down and I came in. That's three days.

units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: Three days of slow ahead is murder on fuel economy, if anyone's counting, which the office is. The engines are fine. I've cleaned the forward flood lenses twice today, because the salt film on them cuts the beam by a good third, and in this muck you want every lumen you can get.

units.author: lineman_garvey
units.text: Salt film's the thing, Seth, you're right. Same on our insulators after a long fog. We'll be washing the Gilliver feeder in a week or two if this keeps up, before the first proper frost. The Lisle job this morning was a cable joint, not the line. Tess did half the work and all the talking to residents. She's good.

units.author: lineman_tess
units.text: Thanks, Garvey. Question for the room, since I'm learning: does fog this thick ever trip anything on the overhead line by itself, or is it always the salt afterwards? Garvey says always afterwards. The trip log for Gilliver is clean all week, for what it's worth, not a flicker.

units.title: lisle pier, evening report
units.author: lisle_crew_ada
units.text: evening report from Lisle... pier lights on at five, all six working, I checked each one twice. last boat in 41 minutes late. nobody on the slip, nobody near it, I stood at the top with my tea till the boat came. Mrs Penrose finished a sleeve. ha, anyway, quiet one

units.author: ferry_mate_kerris
units.text: Thank you, Ada. Saw your lights from three cables off tonight, which in this is a small miracle. It makes a big difference coming in to a slip you can see the whole length of, top to water. Gilliver should have that. Kettle was very welcome.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: An aside, but a practical one: if a slip is lit evenly to the water line, a crew can see a person and judge distance. If only the top is lit, the foot of the slip becomes a dark stage with a bright fog behind it, which is the worst case for misjudging anything. Ada's pier is a good model.
